newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Sleepy Australian stocks close little changed.
newsitem.headline: Sleepy Australian stocks close little changed.

text.p: A sleepy Australian share market ended a dull day barely higher on Tuesday with hesitant investors reluctant to commit funds to a drifting market.
By 4.25 p.m. (0625 GMT), the All Ordinaries index was up 2.9 points at 2,368.9.
June share price index futures were seven points higher at 2,359, a 9.9 point discount to the index.

The day's trade was an arm wrestle between the market's two components with a marginally firmer industrials grouping just overcoming a resources sector feeling the pressure of offshore falls in metal prices.
Activity was slow with turnover by value failing to crack the A$600 million mark.
"It's been very flat," said dealer Justin Hondris of Hartley Poynton, echoing similar comments made throughout the day by other market participants.
"There has been no real excitement today."
The big banks spent the day adrift with a modest if unconvincing rally ahead of Wednesday's release of the Wallis report into the financial system helping the market off its early lows.

Sector leader National Australia Bank added 1.2 percent to A$15.72, while oft-mentioned takeover targets in any financial sector changes, ANZ Bank and Westpac Banking Corporation closed mixed. ANZ Bank lost seven cents to A$8.00 while Westpac added five cents to A$6.87.
Giant retailer Coles Myer Ltd topped turnover with 7.5 million shares traded as the company went ex-dividend 12 cents.
Its shares ended seven cents lower at A$5.90.
Rises and falls were evenly matched, while about 32 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
FUTURES/OPTIONS - Options trade picked up somewhat after several days of light activity while futures trade was moderate.
Total options traded 43,138 (31,684)
Turnover in June SPI contracts totalled 6,212 (7,508)

In other local markets, Australian bond yields finished above the day's lows as the market absorbed today's A$600 million T-bond tender, but the market was seen well-placed to maintain the current rally.
By 4.55 p.m. (0655 GMT), 10 year T-bonds were yielding 7.96 percent, down from Monday's 7.98 percent.
The Australian dollar staged a late bounce on Tuesday, staving off bearish pressure to end local trade slightly higher after earlier carving out fresh six week lows.
By 4.55 p.m. (0230 GMT), the Australian dollar was at S$0.7777/87 from a Monday's local finish of US$0.7754/59.
